items.title: Why kindness matters
items.prompt: Write a paragraph of about 100 words about the importance of kindness in daily life.
items.model: Kindness is one of the most important qualities in our daily life. First, a kind word can change someone's whole day. For example, when a student helps a classmate who does not understand a lesson, both of them feel happier and more confident. Besides, kindness builds trust between people. A neighbour who offers help in a difficult time becomes a friend for years. Moreover, kind people are usually calmer and more positive, because helping others gives them a sense of purpose. In short, kindness costs nothing, but it makes our homes, schools and communities stronger and friendlier places.

items.title: Advice about a machine
items.prompt: Your cousin wants to buy a new laptop for school. Write an email to him (about 100 words) giving advice on what to think about before buying it.
points: Ask what he needs it for
Suggest checking reviews or asking an expert
items.model:
Dear Karim,

I heard that you are planning to buy a laptop for school, so I am writing to give you some advice.

First, think about what you will use it for. If you only need it for homework and the internet, you do not need an expensive model. Second, compare prices and check the quality, such as the battery life and the screen. Do not choose the cheapest one without reading about it. Finally, read some reviews online or ask a computer teacher for his opinion.

I hope this helps. Let me know what you decide.

Best wishes,
Omar

items.title: Protect our environment
items.prompt: Write an article for your school magazine (about 150 words) about what students can do to protect the environment.
items.model:
Small Steps, Big Change

Our planet is facing serious problems, such as pollution and climate change. However, students can play an important part in protecting it.

First of all, we can reduce the waste we produce. Instead of buying plastic bottles every day, we can use a reusable bottle. We can also recycle paper and use both sides of our notebooks. Secondly, saving water and energy is easy. Turning off the tap while we brush our teeth and switching off the lights when we leave a room will save a lot over a year.

In addition, we can take part in school activities such as planting trees and cleaning the streets near our school.

In conclusion, protecting the environment is not only the job of governments. If every student makes a small effort, our future will be much greener.

items.title: A day by the sea
items.prompt: Write a story (about 120 words) that ends with the sentence: "That was the day I learned to respect the sea."
points: Where you were and with whom
items.model: Last summer, my family and I spent a day at the beach. The sun was shining, and my little brother and I were playing near the water. Suddenly, a strong wave pulled his ball far from the shore. Without thinking, I swam after it. After a few minutes, I realised that I was too far from the beach and that the water was getting deeper. I felt afraid, but a lifeguard saw me and swam quickly to help. He brought me safely back to the sand, where my parents were waiting anxiously. They hugged me tightly, and I thanked the lifeguard many times. From then on, I always swim in safe areas and follow the rules. That was the day I learned to respect the sea.

items.title: The value of exercise
items.prompt: Write a paragraph of about 100 words on the benefits of regular exercise for teenagers.
items.model: Regular exercise is very useful for teenagers. To begin with, it keeps the body strong and healthy. Walking, swimming or playing football for thirty minutes a day improves the heart and helps us to sleep well. Besides, exercise is good for the mind. It reduces stress before exams and gives us more energy for studying. Moreover, team sports teach us patience, cooperation and how to accept defeat. For these reasons, I advise every student to find a sport that he enjoys and to practise it regularly. A healthy body usually leads to a happy and focused mind.

items.title: Invitation to a friend
items.prompt: You are organising a small trip to a park with your classmates on Friday. Write an email (about 100 words) inviting your friend Hassan.
items.model:
Dear Hassan,

How are you? I am writing to invite you to a small trip to Al-Azhar Park with some of our classmates this Friday.

We will meet in front of the school gate at 9 a.m. and go together by microbus. Please bring a bottle of water, a snack and a ball if you have one. We are also planning to play some board games under the trees, so bring one if you can.

I really hope you can come. Please reply by Thursday so that I know how many people to expect.

Best wishes,
Ahmed

items.title: Missing the flight
items.prompt: Write a story (about 120 words) beginning with: "I woke up late on the day of my flight."
items.model: I woke up late on the day of my flight. I looked at the clock and jumped out of bed, because the plane was leaving in two hours. I grabbed my suitcase and called a taxi, but the traffic was terrible. While we were waiting in a long queue of cars, I started to worry that I would miss it. Finally, I decided to get out and run to the metro station. When I arrived at the airport, the check-in desk was almost closed. Luckily, a kind employee helped me and I boarded the plane a few minutes before the doors closed. I sat down, breathing hard, and promised myself that I would always set two alarms.

items.title: A visit to a museum
items.prompt: Write an article (about 150 words) for your school magazine about why young people should visit museums and historical places.
points: Why it is better than reading
items.model:
Walking Through History

Many young people spend their free time on their phones, but visiting a museum can be a much more exciting experience.

First, museums teach us about the past in a real way. When we see an ancient statue or a piece of papyrus with our own eyes, we understand how people lived and worked thousands of years ago. This is much more memorable than a page in a textbook.

Secondly, historical places make us proud of our culture. Egypt has some of the most famous monuments in the world, and knowing their stories helps us to value and protect them.

Finally, a trip to a museum with friends or family is a pleasant and cheap way to spend a day.

I strongly advise every student to visit at least one museum this year. You will return home with new ideas and a better understanding of your country.

items.title: Exploring space
items.prompt: Write a paragraph of about 100 words on whether the exploration of space is worth the money.
items.model: In my opinion, exploring space is worth the money. First, space research gives us useful technology. Satellites help us to forecast the weather, use maps on our phones and communicate with people around the world. Second, studying other planets teaches us about our own. Scientists learn how climates change and how to protect the Earth. Moreover, space missions inspire young people to study science and to dream big. Of course, the money could also be spent on hospitals and schools, but both are important. To sum up, discovering the universe brings knowledge and benefits that will last for generations.

items.title: Thanking a host
items.prompt: You stayed with a friend's family for a weekend in another city. Write an email (about 100 words) to thank them.
items.model:
Dear Mr. and Mrs. Samir,

I am writing to thank you for the wonderful weekend I spent with your family. You welcomed me so warmly that I felt at home from the first minute.

I especially enjoyed the dinner on Friday evening. The food was delicious, and I loved the stories that you told us afterwards. The trip to the old market with Adel was also great fun.

I would be very happy to welcome you in Ismailia one day, so please let me know when you are free.

Thank you again for your kindness.

Yours sincerely,
Mina

items.title: The mysterious book
items.prompt: Write a story (about 120 words) about a student who finds an old book in the school library.
items.model: One afternoon, Laila was looking for a book in the school library when she noticed an old, dusty one at the back of a shelf. Its cover was dark blue and had no title. She opened it carefully and found handwritten stories inside. They were written many years ago by a student of the school. One of them was about a girl who dreamed of becoming a doctor. Laila read until the library closed. Then she decided to show the book to her teacher, who was amazed. The school put it in a glass case at the entrance, and Laila became the girl who found a treasure of words.

items.title: Choosing the right university subject
items.prompt: Write an article (about 150 words) giving advice to Secondary 3 students on how to choose a university subject.
points: Think about your interests and skills
items.model:
Choosing Your Future

Soon, many of you will have to choose a university subject. This decision will affect your whole life, so you should take it seriously.

First, think about what you enjoy and what you are good at. A student who loves solving problems may succeed in engineering, while one who enjoys helping others may prefer medicine or teaching.

Secondly, ask for advice. Talk to your parents and teachers, and speak to people who already work in the field you are interested in. They can tell you what the job is really like.

Finally, do not choose a subject only because your friends have chosen it or because it sounds impressive. What suits them may not suit you.

In conclusion, a wise choice is based on interests, skills and good information. If you follow this advice, you will be more likely to enjoy your studies and your career.
